title: Akshay Kumar Turns Villain Against a Blind Saif Ali Khan. Their First Film Together in 17 Years Drops Its Teaser Tonight.
excerpt: Priyadarshan's psychological thriller reunites the Hera Pheri stars minus the laughs — and Akshay says it completes his 'unintentional trilogy' after Insaan and Jaanwar.
body:
There is a moment in every big star's career when the audience stops seeing the person and starts seeing the character. For **Akshay Kumar**, that moment might arrive tonight.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=rR2nTe_tl8Q</youtube>

The teaser for **Haiwaan** — a dark, psychological crime thriller directed by **Priyadarshan** — drops at 8 PM IST on July 15, and it promises something fans have waited years to see: Akshay Kumar playing a cold-blooded, ruthless killer. Not an anti-hero. Not a conflicted cop. A proper villain, the kind who makes you lean back in your seat.

Opposite him is **Saif Ali Khan**, playing a blind man caught in the crosshairs of a predator he cannot see. The setup alone is enough to sell tickets.

## Seventeen Years in the Making

Akshay and Saif haven't shared a screen since their comedic heyday — *Main Khiladi Tu Anari*, *Yeh Dillagi*, and the beloved chaos of *Hera Pheri*. That last film, also directed by Priyadarshan, remains the gold standard for Hindi comedy. Now the same director is bringing the same duo back, but stripping away every trace of humour and replacing it with menace.

> "Bahut Hasaa Liya. Ab Kal Se Haiwaniyat Shuru." — Akshay Kumar, on social media

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaxtS1uBCoH/

The message — *"You've laughed enough. Now the savagery begins"* — is both a tease and a thesis statement. Akshay has spent the better part of the last decade in patriotic dramas and family entertainers. This is a deliberate pivot.

## The 'Unintentional Trilogy'

In a recent interview with Hindustan Times, Akshay revealed that he sees Haiwaan as the final piece of an accidental pattern. He's already done *Insaan* and *Jaanwar* — the human and the animal. Now comes *Haiwaan*, the beast.

> "It's not just about being bad for the sake of it. There's a layered complexity to this character that I'm really excited to explore." — Akshay Kumar

That complexity may come from the film's rumoured source material. Industry whispers suggest Haiwaan is a Hindi adaptation of Priyadarshan's own Malayalam masterpiece **Oppam** (2016), which starred Mohanlal as a blind man who becomes the sole witness — through sound and instinct — to a murder in his apartment building. If the reports hold, Saif's character won't just be a victim; he'll be the one hunting.

## A Cast Built for Tension

Beyond the two leads, the film packs a sharp ensemble. **Boman Irani**, another Priyadarshan regular, returns in what is expected to be a pivotal supporting role. **Saiyami Kher** — fresh from her acclaimed work in *Ghoomer* and the *Breathe* franchise — and **Shriya Pilgaonkar**, who has quietly built one of the most interesting resumes in Indian streaming (*Mirzapur*, *The Broken News*), round out the core cast.

The film is produced by **KVN Productions** and **Thespian Films**, with a release locked for **September 11, 2026**.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who grew up rewinding the *Hera Pheri* DVD at family gatherings, this reunion hits different. The nostalgia is real, but the promise is that Haiwaan won't trade on it. Priyadarshan has always been a different filmmaker when he works in darker territory — think *Kanchivaram*, think *Virasat* — and this appears to be that version of him.

Akshay at 58 playing a villain with conviction, Saif at 55 channelling the quiet intensity that made *Omkara* unforgettable, and Priyadarshan orchestrating the whole thing without a single pratfall in sight.

Watch the teaser tonight. This one might surprise you.
